draft.title: Australia's aid program
card: Australia's government gives aid to other countries to support their health, development and wellbeing.
The program is managed by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), a government department.
Most of the aid goes to countries in the Indo-Pacific, the region of the Pacific Islands and South-East Asia that is close to Australia.
Some of the aid is given directly to another government. Some is passed on through other bodies, such as UN agencies and non-government organisations.
draft.remember: DFAT manages Australia's aid, and most of it goes to the Indo-Pacific.

a.q: Which Australian government department manages the aid program?
opts: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
Department of Health and Aged Care
Department of Education
Department of Home Affairs
a.why: DFAT manages Australia's aid program. The Department of Health and Aged Care is tempting because the aid supports health, but its main work is health within Australia.
a.clue: Think of the department that deals with other countries.

b.q: Which region receives most of Australia's aid?
opts: The Indo-Pacific
Western Europe
North America
South America
b.why: Most of Australia's aid goes to the Indo-Pacific, which includes the Pacific Islands and South-East Asia. Other regions get aid too, but they are not the main focus.
b.clue: Look at the region closest to Australia.

a.best: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

problems.detail: The card defines the Indo-Pacific as 'the region of the Pacific Islands and South-East Asia'. In DFAT's usage it also includes South Asia and the Indian Ocean region, and Australia gives significant aid to countries such as Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. Say 'including' rather than giving it as the whole definition.
The clue 'the department that deals with other countries' points straight to Foreign Affairs, so students can answer without knowing the idea.
The clue 'the region closest to Australia' gives the answer away. The distractors (Western Europe, South America, North America) are far-off rich regions that no student would pick.
Both questions are very easy recall for Year 12. Question b in particular has implausible distractors, so it tests almost nothing at this level.

proposal.title: Australia's aid program
card: Australia's aid program is support from the Australian Government to help other countries improve health, reduce poverty and build development. It is also called official development assistance.
The program is managed by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT). DFAT also runs Australia's relations and trade with other countries.

Most of the aid goes to the Indo-Pacific, including Pacific Island countries such as Papua New Guinea and South-East Asian countries such as Indonesia. Some also goes to South Asia, such as Bangladesh, and smaller amounts go elsewhere.

Australia focuses on the Indo-Pacific because these countries are its neighbours. Their health, stability and prosperity can affect Australia too, for example through diseases that spread across borders.
proposal.remember: Australia's aid is run by DFAT and centred on its Indo-Pacific neighbours, whose wellbeing can affect Australia too.

a.q: Which statement about Australia's aid program is accurate?
opts: DFAT manages it, and most goes to the Indo-Pacific
DFAT manages it, and most goes to Africa
The UN manages it, and most goes to the Indo-Pacific
The UN manages it, and most goes to the Middle East
a.why: DFAT, an Australian Government department, manages the aid, and most of it goes to the Indo-Pacific. The UN options are tempting because the UN is linked with aid, but it does not run Australia's own program.
a.clue: Check both parts: who runs it, and where most of it goes.

b.q: Timor-Leste gets Australian aid to strengthen its health system. Why does Australia focus its aid on countries like this?
opts: Its neighbours' health and stability can affect Australia
The UN requires donors to fund countries in their region
Australia gives aid only to countries it trades with
Indo-Pacific countries are the only ones with low incomes
b.why: Timor-Leste is one of Australia's Indo-Pacific neighbours, and problems such as disease can cross borders, so its health matters to Australia too. The UN option is tempting, but Australia chooses its own focus. Aid also goes to other regions, so low incomes are not only found in the Indo-Pacific.
b.clue: Think about what links a neighbour's health to Australia's own.
